20261119-physics-h1.s.s1.prompt: Two eggs of the same mass are dropped from the same height, one onto a cement floor and the other onto a soft cushion. Which comparison of physical quantities, from the moment each egg touches the surface until it stops, is correct?
20261119-physics-h1.s.s1.explain: Because the change in momentum ($\Delta p$) of the two eggs is the same, the impulse ($I = F\Delta t$) is identical. The cushion lengthens the collision time $\Delta t$, reducing the average impact force $F = \frac{I}{\Delta t}$, so the egg does not break.
20261119-physics-h1.s.s1.hint.0: Since they fall from the same height, the velocity just before impact and the velocity change to rest (change in momentum = impulse) are the same.
20261119-physics-h1.s.s1.hint.1: The soft cushion deforms and lengthens the collision time (Δt).

20261121-physics-h1-1.s.s1.explain: The initial momentum is $p_1 = 0.5 \times 30 = +15\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$ and the final momentum is $p_2 = 0.5 \times (-40) = -20\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. The magnitude of the impulse is $|\Delta p| = |-20 - 15| = 35\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$.

20261122-physics-h1-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced mechanics] An object of mass 1 kg is launched horizontally at 20 m/s from the edge of an 80 m high cliff. How far does it travel horizontally before reaching the ground? (Use g = 10 m/s² and ignore air resistance.)
20261122-physics-h1-1.s.s1.explain: The vertical fall time is $80 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \implies t^2 = 16 \implies t = 4$ s. Since horizontal motion is uniform, the horizontal distance is $x = v_x t = 20\text{ m/s} \times 4\text{ s} = 80\text{ m}$.
20261122-physics-h1-1.s.s1.hint.0: First find the fall time t: h = (1/2) g t² → 80 = (1/2) × 10 × t²
20261122-physics-h1-1.s.s1.hint.1: Then calculate the horizontal distance x = v_x × t.

20261122-physics-h1-2.thinking.0: What is the scientific reason that
20261122-physics-h1-2.s.s1.prompt: What is the scientific reason that OLED (organic light-emitting diode) displays used in the latest smartphones and TVs are thinner and have better contrast than conventional LCDs?
20261122-physics-h1-2.s.s1.explain: OLED uses thin films of organic semiconductor that emit light by themselves when current flows, so a thick backlight unit is unnecessary, and by turning pixels off it achieves perfect black, giving infinite contrast.
20261122-physics-h1-2.s.s1.hint.0: LCDs require a backlight that shines light from behind.
20261122-physics-h1-2.s.s1.hint.1: In OLED, every single pixel is self-emissive.
20261122-physics-h1-2.s.s1.o.o0: Because they use self-emitting organic compound elements that produce light on their own without a separate backlight

20261122-physics-h1-2.steps.0.prompt: What is the scientific reason that OLED (organic light-emitting diode) displays used in the latest smartphones and TVs are thinner and have better contrast than conventional LCDs?
20261122-physics-h1-2.steps.0.explain: OLED uses thin films of organic semiconductor that emit light by themselves when current flows, so a thick backlight unit is unnecessary, and by turning pixels off it achieves perfect black, giving infinite contrast.
